hints.content:
This is the formula for the average rate of change of a function $f$ over the interval $[a,b]$:

$\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$

We will need to know the values of $g(3)$ and $g(10)$ to find the slope.

$\begin{align}
g(3)&=7-8(3)
\\\\
&=-17
\\\\\\
g(10)&=7-8(10)
\\\\
&=-73
\\\\\\
\dfrac{g(10)-g(3)}{10-3}&=\dfrac{-73-(-17)}{7}
\\\\
&=-8
\end{align}$

**The average rate of change of $g$ over the interval $[3,10]$ is $-8$.**

Notice that the average rate of change is calculated just like the slope of the [[☃ definition 1]] that intersects the graph of the function at the interval's endpoints.

![Function g is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 1 to 11. The graph consists of a line. The line starts in quadrant 2 and moves downward into quadrant 4, through a point at (3, g of 3) and then a point at (10, g of 10), and ends in quadrant 4. A secant line connects the 2 points, on the line.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/9ed0025fa6de6703c3849f1713aea535032c37da)

options.definition: A **secant line** is a line that intersects a curve at $2$ or more points.
